title: What are the values of these powers of minus numbers and zero?
description: Six powers are worked out one by one: powers of minus four, minus one and minus two, and powers of zero. The sign of each answer comes from counting the minus signs. Keeko's doubt is that the minus signs vanish.
teaching_notes: One idea: a power of a minus number has a minus answer when the exponent is odd and a plus answer when it is even, and zero to any power stays zero. Watch for students who think the minus signs vanish when a power is worked out.

video_script.why: The child can work out a power of a plus number and now meets minus bases and zero, where the sign of the answer depends on how many minus signs are multiplied.
video_script.substitution: The book's own six powers, with minus four, minus one, minus two and zero.
video_script.anchor: the six powers written in a row on the board, each one opened out into its repeated multiplication
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the minus signs vanish, so minus four to the power three is plus sixty four. Three minus signs are multiplied, and an odd count leaves one minus sign behind.
video_script.payoff_line: Minus four to the power three is minus sixty four

final_answer.value: (−4)³ is −64, (−1)⁵ is −1, (−1)⁵⁶ is 1, (−2)⁴ is 16, and 0² and 0⁵ are 0
final_answer.spoken: minus four to the power three is minus sixty four, minus one to the power five is minus one, minus one to the power fifty six is one, minus two to the power four is sixteen, and zero squared and zero to the power five are both zero

maths_rules: (−1)⁵ has 5 minus signs, an odd count, so it is −1
(−1)⁵⁶ has 56 minus signs, an even count, so it is 1
slip: the minus signs vanish, giving 64
video_script.design: One idea: count the minus signs to find the sign of the answer. The six powers stay on the board all video; the last multiplication of the first power is left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

marks.one: (−4)³ is opened out into three factors

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, minus four to the power three means three minus fours multiplied.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Minus four times minus four is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Sixteen times minus four is left to find.

beats.on_screen: (−1)⁵: five minus signs, odd, so −1; (−1)⁵⁶: fifty six minus signs, even, so 1

marks.two: the minus signs in (−1)⁵ are counted: five
marks.even: the minus signs in (−1)⁵⁶ are counted: fifty six, an even count, giving 1

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, count the minus signs.
Minus one to the power five has five minus signs, an odd count.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>An odd count gives a negative answer, so the value is minus one.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Minus one to the power fifty six has fifty six minus signs, an even count.
An even count gives a positive answer, so the value is one.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, multiply minus two four times.
Minus two times minus two is four.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Four times minus two is minus eight.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Minus eight times minus two is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, zero times zero is zero.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Zero multiplied five times is zero too.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Minus four to the power three is minus sixty four.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Minus one to the power five is minus one.
Minus one to the power fifty six is one.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Minus two to the power four is sixteen.
Zero squared and zero to the power five are both zero.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: (−4)³ = 64 appears, then is crossed out; three minus signs are drawn, two join into a plus and one minus is left

marks.fix: 64 is crossed out and the three minus signs are shown, with two joining into a plus

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the minus signs vanish, so minus four to the power three is plus sixty four.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two of the three minus signs join to give a positive.
One minus sign is left behind, so the answer stays negative.
